topic_tag: tourist VAT refund paid by a card that converts currency
subskill: tax included in a price, currency conversion
prompt: In a certain country, the posted price of a coat is 196.80 euros. This posted price includes a value-added tax (VAT) of 25% of the pre-tax price. A visitor is charged the posted price minus a tourist refund, where the refund is the VAT included in the posted price less a 30% service charge that the refund agency keeps from that VAT. The visitor pays with a card that converts euros to dollars at 1.078 dollars per euro and then adds a fee of 1.5% of the converted dollar amount. To the nearest cent, how many dollars in total does the visitor's card charge for the coat?
explanation: The pre-tax price is 196.80 / 1.25 = 157.44 euros, so the VAT included is 196.80 - 157.44 = 39.36 euros. The agency keeps 30% of it, so the refund is 0.70(39.36) = 27.552 euros, and the visitor is charged 196.80 - 27.552 = 169.248 euros. Converted: 169.248(1.078) = 182.449 dollars; with the 1.5% fee: 182.449(1.015) = 185.19 dollars. The option "177.65" takes the VAT as 25% of the posted price (49.20 euros) instead of 25% of the pre-tax price. The option "202.41" takes the refund as the 30% the agency keeps instead of the 70% it returns. The option "187.07" takes the pre-tax price as 75% of the posted price (147.60 euros) and the VAT as 25% of that (36.90 euros).
quantity_asked: the total dollar amount the card charges: (posted price minus 70% of the included VAT) converted at 1.078 dollars per euro, plus a 1.5% fee.

distractor_kind.177.65: error path: VAT computed as 25% of the posted (tax-included) price, 49.20 euros, instead of the 39.36 euros actually included. (a) not a parameter extreme; strictly inside the bounds (172.27, 215.33). (b) not the full-refund answer 172.27 or the no-refund answer 215.33. (c) one-step estimate 197(1 - 0.2 x 0.7)(1.09) ~ 184 sits between options; every distractor strictly inside (172.27, 215.33). (d) real wrong-base error on a tax-included price.
distractor_kind.202.41: error path: refund taken as the 30% the agency keeps instead of the 70% it returns. (a) no extreme. (b) not the no-refund total 215.33. (c) inside (172.27, 215.33). (d) real complement slip.
distractor_kind.187.07: error path: the pre-tax price found by taking 25% off the posted price (147.60) instead of dividing by 1.25 (157.44), then VAT = 25% of 147.60 = 36.90 euros, a smaller refund. (a) no extreme. (b) not an edge value. (c) inside (172.27, 215.33), 1.9 dollars from the key. (d) real wrong-base error (removing a markup as a discount).

bounds: charge > 172.27 (refund of the whole included VAT, the largest possible refund)
mechanism: VAT refund less a service charge
arith_class_check: No. All four are two-decimal dollar amounts between 177 and 203; no integrality or divisibility property isolates 185.19.
one_sided_check: key interior (one distractor under, two over).
interior_parity_check: Interior by value: 185.19 and 187.07, both three-digit amounts with two non-zero decimal places; neither is rounder.
trap_check: Clauses: "includes a VAT of 25% of the pre-tax price" - taking 25% of the posted price over-states the VAT and pushes the charge DOWN (177.65); "less a 30% service charge" - taking the refund as 30% pushes it UP (202.41); "adds a fee of 1.5%" - ignoring it pushes DOWN (182.45, not an option); removing the 25% tax as a 25% discount pushes UP (187.07); the refund itself - ignoring it pushes UP (215.33, not an option). No distractor comes from ignoring a clause; errors push both ways.

187.07.step: pre-tax price from the posted price

VAT is 25% of the pre-tax price (included in the posted price)
agency keeps 30% of the VAT

1.5% card fee

topic_tag: ferry crossing timed from speeds in knots over a route in mixed miles
subskill: nautical and statute miles, two-leg travel time
prompt: A ferry route is 38.5 statute miles long. The first 2.4 nautical miles of the route are inside a harbor, where the ferry travels at a constant 5 knots; for the rest of the route it travels at a constant 17 knots. A speed of 1 knot is 1 nautical mile per hour, and 1 nautical mile = 1.151 statute miles. To the nearest tenth of a minute, how many minutes does the ferry take to travel the whole route?
explanation: The harbor leg is 2.4 nautical miles at 5 nautical miles per hour: 2.4/5 h = 28.8 minutes. In statute miles the harbor leg is 2.4(1.151) = 2.762 miles, so the open-water leg is 38.5 - 2.762 = 35.738 statute miles. At 17 knots = 17(1.151) = 19.567 statute miles per hour, it takes 35.738/19.567 h = 109.59 minutes. Total: about 138.4 minutes. The option "139.5" subtracts 2.4 directly from 38.5, mixing nautical and statute miles. The option "142.7" converts the harbor distance to 2.762 statute miles but then divides it by 5 knots as if they were the same unit. The option "154.9" leaves the open-water speed as 17 statute miles per hour.
quantity_asked: the total travel time in minutes: 2.4 nautical miles at 5 knots plus the remaining 38.5 - 2.4(1.151) statute miles at 17 knots.

distractor_kind.139.5: error path: 2.4 nautical miles subtracted from 38.5 statute miles without converting, so the open-water leg is 36.1 instead of 35.738 miles. (a) not a parameter extreme. (b) not the no-harbor time 118.1. (c) cheap bounds: time > 118.1 (whole route at 17 knots), time < 401 (whole route at 5 knots); one-step estimate 29 + 36/(17 x 1.15) h ~ 29 + 110 = 139 has a resolution of several minutes, and 139.5 is inside it. (d) real unit-mixing error.
distractor_kind.142.7: error path: harbor distance converted to statute miles but divided by the speed in knots. (a) no extreme. (b) not an edge. (c) inside (118.1, 401). (d) real mixed-unit rate error.
distractor_kind.154.9: error path: 17 knots used as 17 statute miles per hour on the open-water leg. (a) not a parameter extreme of the item (the harbor leg and the subtraction still use 1.151). (b) not an edge. (c) inside (118.1, 401). (d) real unit error.

mechanism: knots to statute miles per hour
harbor length in nautical miles, route in statute miles
slow harbor leg then open water

topic_tag: unit price under a second-item discount versus a bonus-size jar

Store B sells a jar labeled 30 ounces for $7.89, and during a promotion each of its jars contains 15% more peanut butter than the labeled amount, at the same price. A customer buying exactly 2 jars at Store A pays the sale price for the second jar. Based on the cost per ounce, how many cents more per ounce does the peanut butter cost at Store B than at Store A for this customer, to the nearest tenth of a cent?
explanation: At Store A, two jars cost 5.76 + 0.60(5.76) = 9.216 dollars for 48 ounces, or 19.20 cents per ounce. At Store B, one jar holds 30(1.15) = 34.5 ounces for 789 cents, or about 22.87 cents per ounce. The difference is about 3.7 cents per ounce. The option "3.2" treats 15% more peanut butter as 15% off the price (6.7065 dollars for 30 ounces, 22.36 cents per ounce). The option "6.1" charges 40% of the price for the second jar at Store A instead of 60% (16.80 cents per ounce). The option "2.3" prices the second jar at Store A as 5.76 / 1.40 dollars, treating 40% off as dividing by 1.40 (20.57 cents per ounce).
quantity_asked: Store B's cost per ounce (789 cents over 34.5 ounces) minus Store A's cost per ounce for two jars with the second at 40% off, in cents.

Using 1 yard = 0.9144 meter, what is the coach's predicted time for the race, to the nearest second?
explanation: The race is 1500 / 0.9144 = 1640.42 yards, or 16.4042 hundreds of yards. The race pace is 92(1.02) = 93.84 seconds per 100 yards, so the swim takes 16.4042(93.84) = 1539.37 seconds; subtracting 3.0 seconds gives about 1536 seconds. The option "1476" makes the race pace 2% faster (92 x 0.98) instead of 2% slower. The option "1322" reads the pace 1 minute 32 seconds as 1.32 minutes (79.2 seconds). The option "1284" converts the wrong way, multiplying 1,500 by 0.9144 to get 1,371.6 yards.

topic_tag: home charging time for an electric car with a tapered charge rate
subskill: energy over power, efficiency, two rate segments
prompt: An electric car's battery stores 66 kilowatt-hours (kWh) when full and is now at 24% of full. Its home charger draws power from the wall at a constant 7.2 kilowatts (kW) until the battery reaches 80% of full, and then at a constant 2.6 kW until the battery reaches 90% of full, when charging stops. Only 90% of the energy drawn from the wall is stored in the battery. (A charger drawing 1 kW for 1 hour draws 1 kWh.) To the nearest hundredth of an hour, how many hours does the charging take?
explanation: From 24% to 80% the battery must store 0.56(66) = 36.96 kWh. It stores 0.90(7.2) = 6.48 kWh per hour, so this takes 36.96 / 6.48 = 5.704 hours. From 80% to 90% it must store 0.10(66) = 6.6 kWh at 0.90(2.6) = 2.34 kWh per hour, which takes 2.821 hours. Total: about 8.52 hours. The option "8.44" accounts for the loss by multiplying the stored energy by 1.10 instead of dividing it by 0.90. The option "8.24" applies the 90% efficiency to the first segment but not to the slower segment above 80%. The option "9.47" applies the 90% efficiency twice, dividing the needed energy by 0.90 and also using only 90% of the charger's power.
quantity_asked: the total charging time in hours: 36.96 kWh stored at 0.90 x 7.2 kWh per hour plus 6.6 kWh stored at 0.90 x 2.6 kWh per hour.

topic_tag: mass of a scaled bronze copy of a wooden sculpture
subskill: scale factor cubed, density ratio, pounds to kilograms
prompt: A solid wooden sculpture is weighed while standing on its oak base, and the scale reads 1,520 pounds. Weighed without the base, the sculpture is 165 pounds lighter. A foundry will cast a solid bronze copy of the sculpture alone in which every length is 3/8 of the corresponding length of the original. The wood has a density of 0.68 gram per cubic centimeter, and the bronze has a density of 8.8 grams per cubic centimeter. Given that 1 pound = 0.4536 kilogram, what is the mass, to the nearest kilogram, of the bronze copy?
explanation: The sculpture alone is 1,520 - 165 = 1,355 pounds, or 1,355(0.4536) = 614.63 kilograms. Every length is 3/8 of the original, so the volume is (3/8)^3 = 27/512 of the original, and a wooden copy would have mass 614.63(27/512) = 32.41 kilograms. Bronze is 8.8/0.68 times as dense as the wood, so the bronze copy has mass 32.41(8.8/0.68) = 419 kilograms. The option "522" adds the 165 pounds instead of subtracting them. The option "1119" scales by (3/8)^2, as for an area. The option "2039" divides by 0.4536 instead of multiplying.
quantity_asked: the bronze copy's mass in kilograms: (1,520 - 165) pounds x 0.4536, times (3/8)^3, times 8.8/0.68.

distractor_kind.522: error path: "165 pounds lighter" applied as an addition (a sign slip), sculpture taken as 1,685 pounds. (a) not a parameter extreme. (b) not the with-base value 471 or the wooden-copy value 32. (c) one-step estimate 615 x 0.053 x 12.9 ~ 420, resolution a few percent; 522 is strictly inside (32, 7954). (d) real sign slip.
distractor_kind.1119: error path: the length ratio squared instead of cubed (area scaling for a mass). (a) no extreme. (b) not an edge. (c) inside (32, 7954). (d) real square-cube error.
distractor_kind.2039: error path: pounds converted by dividing by 0.4536 instead of multiplying. (a) no extreme. (b) not an edge. (c) inside. (d) real inverted conversion.

bounds: mass > 32.4 (a copy in the same wood; bronze is denser)
mechanism: weighed with and without a base
arith_class_check: No. All four are whole kilogram values (419, 522, 1119, 2039); none is a multiple of 10 or 25, and no option is a fixed multiple of another by a stem number.
one_sided_check: key smallest; the distractors come from a sign slip (lighter read as heavier), a squared scale factor and an inverted conversion. Natural errors on the other side: inverting the density ratio (x 0.68/8.8) gives 2.50, and leaving the wood density in place gives 32.41; both below the key.
interior_parity_check: Interior by value: 522 and 1119, both whole numbers with non-zero last digits; neither is rounder.
cheap_bound_check: Cheapest one-sided bounds: more than 32.4 (same-wood copy) and less than 7,954 (full-size bronze); every option is inside. The one-step estimate needs the 165-pound subtraction and the cube; 522 is 103 kg (25%) above the key, a resolution no estimate that skips the base step reaches.
trap_check: Clauses: "165 pounds lighter" - adding pushes UP (522), ignoring it pushes UP (471, not an option); "every length is 3/8" - squaring pushes UP (1119), ignoring pushes UP (7,954, not an option); "0.68 ... 8.8" densities - inverting pushes DOWN (2.50, not an option), ignoring pushes DOWN (32.41, not an option); "1 pound = 0.4536 kilogram" - dividing pushes UP (2039), ignoring pushes UP (925, not an option). No distractor comes from ignoring a clause.

1119.error_type: other: length ratio squared, not cubed

stated_rules.rule: sculpture is 165 pounds lighter without the base
every length is 3/8 of the original
wood 0.68 g/cm3, bronze 8.8 g/cm3
1 pound = 0.4536 kilogram

topic_tag: brewed coffee yield after grounds retain water and some water evaporates
subskill: ratio by mass, retained amount, percent loss
prompt: A cafe brews coffee using 1 gram of ground coffee for every 16 grams of water. For one batch it uses 870 grams of water and the matching amount of ground coffee. During brewing, the wet grounds keep 2.2 grams of water for every gram of ground coffee, and 3% of the 870 grams of water evaporates. All other water ends up as brewed coffee, and after brewing 40 grams of hot water is stirred into the brewed coffee. (Ignore the mass of anything dissolved from the grounds.) To the nearest tenth of a gram, how many grams of coffee does the batch produce, including the added hot water?
explanation: The batch uses 870/16 = 54.375 grams of coffee. The grounds keep 2.2(54.375) = 119.625 grams of water, and 0.03(870) = 26.1 grams evaporates. Brewed coffee: 870 - 119.625 - 26.1 = 724.275 grams; with the 40 grams of hot water, 764.3 grams. The option "767.9" takes the 3% of the water left after the grounds' share (750.375) instead of 3% of 870. The option "768.5" removes the 3% by dividing 750.375 by 1.03. The option "771.3" takes the coffee as 1/17 of 870 grams (51.18 grams) instead of 870/16.
quantity_asked: the grams of coffee produced: 870 minus the 2.2 x 54.375 grams kept by the grounds minus 3% of 870 grams, plus 40 grams of added water.

distractor_kind.767.9: error path: the 3% taken of the water left after the grounds' share (750.375) instead of the 870 grams poured. (a) not a parameter extreme. (b) not the no-evaporation value 790.4 or any edge; strictly inside (0, 790.4). (c) one-step estimate 870 - 2.2(54) - 26 + 40 ~ 765, resolution a few grams; 727.9 is inside. (d) real wrong-base percent error.
distractor_kind.768.5: error path: the 3% removed by dividing by 1.03 (applied to the water left after the grounds' share). (a) no extreme. (b) not an edge. (c) inside. (d) real percent-removal error.
distractor_kind.771.3: error path: 1 : 16 read as coffee = 1/17 of the water, giving 51.18 g of coffee and less retained water. (a) no extreme. (b) not an edge. (c) inside (0, 790.4). (d) real part-to-whole ratio error.

771.3.error_kind: ratio part read as part of the whole

bounds: total < 883.9 (no water kept by the grounds)
mechanism: grounds keep 2.2 g water per g
arith_class_check: No. All four are one-decimal gram values between 764 and 772; none is a whole number or a half.
one_sided_check: key smallest; the distractors come from three different errors (the evaporation taken on the wrong base, the evaporation removed by division, the brew ratio read as part of the whole). Natural errors on the other side: taking the 3% of the water plus the coffee (870 + 54.375 grams) gives 762.6, and subtracting the 40 grams instead of adding it gives 684.3, both below the key.
interior_parity_check: Interior by value: 767.9 and 768.5, both three-digit one-decimal values with non-zero decimals; neither is rounder.
cheap_bound_check: Cheapest one-sided bounds: below 790.4 (no evaporation) and below 883.9 (no retention); every option lies below both, so they kill nothing. The one-step estimate ~765 has a resolution of a few grams and does not separate 767.9 or 768.5 from 764.3.
trap_check: Clauses: "3% of the 870 grams of water evaporates" - taking 3% of a smaller base pushes UP (767.9), dividing by 1.03 pushes UP (768.5), taking it of the water plus coffee pushes DOWN (762.6, not an option), ignoring it pushes UP (790.4, not an option); "1 gram ... for every 16 grams of water" - 1/17 pushes UP (771.3); "keep 2.2 grams of water for every gram" - ignoring it pushes UP (883.9, not an option); "40 grams of hot water is stirred in" - ignoring it pushes DOWN (724.3, not an option). grounds keep 2.2 g water per g coffee

topic_tag: scheduled hours for a pipe-laying job from a crew rate in meters
subskill: crew hours from a work rate, length conversion, time adjustments
prompt: A crew usually lays drainage pipe at a rate of 47 meters per hour. A new job requires 1,850 yards of pipe. Because the soil on this job is soft, the crew's working time per meter will be 25% less than usual. The contractor schedules the crew's working time for the job plus an additional 17% of that working time for setup and inspection. Using 1 yard = 0.9144 meter, how many hours does the contractor schedule, to the nearest hundredth of an hour?
explanation: The job is 1850(0.9144) = 1,691.64 meters. At the usual rate this would take 1,691.64 / 47 = 35.992 hours; with 25% less time per meter it takes 0.75(35.992) = 26.994 hours. Adding 17% gives 1.17(26.994) = 31.58 hours. The option "32.52" adds the 17% by dividing by 0.83 instead of multiplying by 1.17. The option "33.11" combines the percents by addition, 35.992(1 - 0.25 + 0.17). The option "37.77" converts yards to meters by dividing by 0.9144 instead of multiplying.
quantity_asked: the scheduled hours: 1,850 yards in meters divided by 47 meters per hour, times 0.75, times 1.17.

distractor_kind.32.52: error path: the 17% added as a division by 0.83 instead of a multiplication by 1.17. (a) not a parameter extreme. (b) not the working time 26.99 or the usual-time value 42.47 or any edge. (c) one-step estimate 1,690/47 ~ 36, x 0.75 ~ 27, x 1.17 ~ 32, resolution about an hour; 32.52 is inside. (d) real wrong-base percent error.

distractor_kind.37.77: error path: yards converted to meters by dividing by 0.9144 instead of multiplying. (a) no extreme. (b) not an edge; inside (26.99, 42.47). (c) inside. (d) real inverted conversion.

mechanism: crew rate in meters per hour
arith_class_check: No. All four are two-decimal hour values between 31 and 38; none is a whole or half number.
one_sided_check: key smallest; the distractors come from three different errors (a margin used for a markup, percents added, an inverted conversion). Natural error on the other side: leaving out the 17% setup allowance gives 26.99, below the key.
interior_parity_check: Interior by value: 32.52 and 33.11, both two-decimal values with non-zero last digits; neither is rounder.
